Good point, I don't see any writes to it either.

I think at one point, it was used to store code actions for warnings being treated as errors so that the code actions could still be performed on them. To go along with that, `push_error` previously was able to accept a list of code actions to use, and those were stored here. In order to minimize edits to the analyzer/parser, the generation of code actions was changed so that they occurred inside of `push_warning`, using the AST node and warning code to determine which ones to generate. `push_error` doesn't receive any of this info, so it doesn't have a way to generate any code actions.

There are two directions I could go with this:

- Create a version of `push_error` that accepts an optional `CodeActionGroup` and applies it to this member. Then, warnings treated as errors will have code actions associated with them. This would be best for users IMO, but it may make the parser a little messier as we'll have an argument for `push_error` that only exists when `TOOLS_ENABLED` is set since `CodeActionGroup` and other code action classes/structs are `EditorLanguage` specific.
- Remove this member declaration for now, as well as associated places in the code where it's read from. Then, warnings treated as errors will not have code actions associated with them (same as current behavior).
Currently correct, although if I go with option 1 in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/121338#discussion_r4028301673, it will be used there

I figured out a third way to accomplish this which avoids adding additional overloads/versions of `push_error()`. Basically, since errors are pushed onto the error list in order and we can thus get the most recent error with `errors.back()->get()`, I was able to introduce a function that is called immediately after `push_error()` and adds the code actions to the error that was just pushed. See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/121338/changes#diff-2472b090d5926cdfdf9227c58051bc8d6821278624979ca1c0a59815b260d7cdL316 for its use, and slightly above that in the diff for its implementation.

Thanks for catching this! Writing the logic out, I think the parentheses are just redundant; my guess is they're left over from an earlier version that we corrected at some point in code review.

As it currently is, with or without the parentheses:
- If this is the last line in the file, OR
  - The next line is indented such that there's space for the button, OR
  - The next line is empty
  
Makes sense to me - these are all conditions that would cause there to be space for the button. Of course, in this case the parentheses are redundant as you said.

---

With your first possibility of what was originally meant:
- If this is the last line in the file, OR
  - The next line is indented such that there's space for the button, AND
  - The next line is empty
  
I don't think the last two conditions can be true simultaneously and thus make their AND'ed value be true, unless `get_line_width()` ignores whitespace. If it's indented, then it shouldn't be empty.

---

Second possibility of what was originally meant:
- If this is the last line in the file, AND
  - The next line is indented such that there's space for the button, OR
  - The next line is empty
 
If this is the last line in the file, then there shouldn't be a next line.

---

With this in mind, I'll remove the parentheses. If there's a flaw in my evaluation of the logic possibilities above, then I can readjust the logic as necessary.

Thank you again! 🙂
I trust your reasoning it sounds logical!
